mainEntity.name: How much does a Renault Captur E-Tech PHEV engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Renault Captur E-Tech PHEV engine replacement typically costs £2,800-£3,800 supply-only for a rebuilt unit, or £2,500-£3,200 for a reconditioned engine, depending on the specific H4M engine code (H4M 630, H4M B6, or H4M 632). Used engine options start from around £1,800. Supply and fit adds approximately 8-12 hours of labour at specialist rates. Note that hybrid system diagnostics and calibration may add additional costs.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of engine problems in a Renault Captur E-Tech PHEV?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common signs include loud engine noise under load or at higher revs, unusually high engine RPM in low gears, loss of power, warning lights on the dashboard, and the engine sounding strained when climbing hills. Some owners also report the petrol engine engaging unpredictably or vibrating excessively.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Renault Captur E-Tech PHEV?

acceptedAnswer.text: This depends entirely on the vehicle's condition and value. With Captur E-Tech PHEV values typically between £16,000-£32,000, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine with warranty is a sound investment for most examples if the car is otherwise in good condition. Always have the hybrid system and battery health checked before committing to engine replacement.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Renault Captur E-Tech PHEV engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical Renault Captur E-Tech PHEV engine replacement takes 2-3 days for the engine swap itself, depending on the workshop's workload. The H4M engine is well-supported with good parts availability. Allow additional time for hybrid system diagnostics, calibration, and final checks.

mainEntity.name: What engine code is in my Renault Captur E-Tech PHEV?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Renault Captur E-Tech PHEV uses the 1.6-litre H4M engine family. The engine code can be found on the engine block, on the vehicle identification plate, or via your VIN using an online decoder. Common codes include H4M 630 (160hp), H4M B6 (160hp), and H4M 632 (143hp).

mainEntity.name: What warranty comes with a Renault Captur E-Tech PHEV replacement engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Every engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. This covers the engine unit against manufacturing defects and failure, providing peace of mind for one of the most significant repairs a Captur E-Tech PHEV owner can undertake. Always confirm exact terms with your chosen supplier. Hybrid system components (electric motors, battery, ECU) may be covered separately.

historyTimeline.h2: Renault Captur E-Tech PHEV - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Renault Captur E-Tech Plug-in Hybrid launched in 2020 as Renault's first rechargeable hybrid model, bringing E-Tech hybrid technology to the compact crossover segment. The powertrain combines a 1.6-litre four-cylinder petrol engine with two electric motors and a 9.8 kWh lithium-ion battery, delivering a cumulative 160hp. This series-parallel hybrid architecture allows the Captur E-Tech PHEV to run on pure electric power for daily commutes (up to 50 km WLTP) while offering the flexibility of hybrid operation for longer journeys.

milestones.description: Renault Captur E-Tech Plug-in Hybrid launched with 1.6-litre petrol engine (H4M 630/H4M B6) and two electric motors, 160hp combined output
9.8 kWh battery pack installed under rear seats, 400V system, 50km electric range
E-Tech 145 variant introduced (H4M 632, 143hp) alongside the 160hp PHEV
Software updates rolled out to address hybrid system behaviour and drivability
Facelift models receive updated infotainment and driver assistance systems
2026 model year Captur full hybrid E-Tech 160 announced, continuing the PHEV powertrain

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Renault Captur E-Tech PHEV is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Renault Captur E-Tech PHEV Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Renault Captur E-Tech PHEV uses a 1.6-litre four-cylinder petrol engine (H4M family) from the Renault-Nissan Alliance, adapted for hybrid operation with two electric motors and a dog-clutch transmission. While the engine itself is a proven unit, the hybrid system introduces additional complexity. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Petrol Engine Noise & NVH Issues - Why the Renault Captur E-Tech PHEV Engine Can Sound Loud
problems.rootCause: Some owners report the petrol engine can be loud and strained, particularly under load, on inclines, or when the engine revs high in low gears. The E-Tech's multimodal clutchless gearbox can sometimes hold gears longer than expected, causing elevated engine RPM. In some cases, software updates have been released to address drivability concerns.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Hybrid system software update to improve gearbox behaviour
repairOptions.longevity: First step; may resolve drivability issues

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Inspection and replacement of worn engine mounts

problems.vehicleValueCheck: Renault Captur E-Tech PHEV values typically sit between £16,000-£32,000 depending on age and mileage. Replacement cost is typically small relative to vehicle value for most examples. Always have the hybrid system diagnosed by a specialist before committing to replacement.
problems.recommendation: If your Captur E-Tech PHEV exhibits loud engine noise or unusual revving, start with a software update from a Renault dealer - this resolves many drivability issues. If the problem persists, have the engine mounts and transmission inspected before considering replacement.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt H4M 630 Renault Captur E-Tech PHEV engine prices

problems.h4: Hybrid System & Transmission Behaviour - Why the Renault Captur E-Tech PHEV Can Feel Unpredictable
problems.rootCause: The E-Tech system uses a clutchless multimodal gearbox developed with Formula 1-derived technology. Some owners report high engine revs, difficulty with gear changes, and the engine staying in low gears on hills. Electrical gremlins and loss of power have also been reported. Renault has issued software updates to address some of these concerns.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full diagnostic scan of hybrid system and transmission
Transmission and hybrid control unit software update
Repair or replacement of multimodal gearbox components

problems.vehicleValueCheck: With Captur E-Tech PHEV values typically £16,000-£32,000, transmission repairs are well within the vehicle's value. For higher-mileage examples, evaluate the cost of repair vs the vehicle's condition.
problems.recommendation: For hybrid system issues, always start with a diagnostic scan and software update - many issues are software-related and can be resolved without mechanical work. If the problem persists, seek a specialist with Renault E-Tech experience.
problems.cta: -> Compare replacement costs for your Renault Captur E-Tech PHEV

problems.h4: Timing Chain System - Preventative Maintenance for the Renault Captur E-Tech PHEV
problems.rootCause: The 1.6-litre H4M engine uses a timing chain (not a belt). While the H4M chain is generally durable, regular oil changes are essential for chain longevity. Unlike the problematic 1.2 TCe engines where chain wear could occur as early as 40,000-60,000 km, the H4M family has a better reliability record.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Inspection of chain tension and condition

repairOptions.longevity: If chain rattle or wear is detected
If chain has failed or caused internal damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: With Captur E-Tech PHEV values typically £16,000-£32,000, timing chain replacement is well within the vehicle's value. For vehicles approaching 100,000 miles, proactive chain replacement is a sensible investment.
problems.recommendation: The H4M timing chain is generally reliable if regular oil changes are maintained. If you hear a rattling noise on cold start, have the chain inspected immediately - early detection prevents catastrophic engine damage.
